questions.q: Which of the following curves represent the variation of coefficient of volume expansion of an ideal gas at constant pressure?
questions.solution:
Volume expansion is the expansion of volume of a gas due to increase in its temperature.
$\therefore$ Coefficient of volume expansion is given as
$\alpha_{V}=\frac{\Delta V}{V \times \Delta T}...(i)$
where, $V=$ real volume of gas,
$\Delta V$ - change in volume
and $\Delta T=$ change in temperature.
From idcal gas cquation,
$p V=n R T \text { or } T=\frac{p V}{n R}...(ii)$
For constant pressure,
$\begin{aligned}
p \Delta V &=n R \Delta T \\
\frac{\Delta V}{\Delta T} &=\frac{n R}{p}...(iii)
\end{aligned}$
From Eqs. (i) and (iii), we get
$\alpha_{V}=\frac{n R}{p V}=\frac{1}{T} \quad[\because \text { From Eq. (ii) }]$
Thus, the variation of $\alpha_{V}$ with temperature is correctly depicted in option (b).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements A and B and identify the correct answers given below.
A. Peltier coefficient is numerically equal to the potential difference across the junctions of the thermocouple through which current is flowing.

B. According to Thomson, energy is neither absorbed nor evolved at the junction of a thermocouple but is observed or evolved only along the lengths of both the conductors.
options: Both A and B are true
Both A and B are false
$\mathrm{A}$ is true but B is false
questions.solution:
Statement A: Peltier coefficient is numerically equal to the potential difference across the junctions of the thermocouple through which current is flowing.
✅ True — By definition, the Peltier coefficient (π) is the amount of emf (potential difference) per unit current at the junction.
Statement B: According to Thomson, energy is neither absorbed nor evolved at the junction of a thermocouple but only along the lengths of both conductors.
❌ False — This is not correct. The Thomson effect states that heat is absorbed or evolved along the length of a conductor carrying current in a temperature gradient, but at the junctions, heat exchange does occur due to the Peltier effect.

Reason : According to Wrichoff a law the absorptivity of a body is equal to its emissivity at a given wavelength.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of \((\mathrm{A})\).
questions.solution:
A good radiator, which emits energy efficiently, will also absorb energy efficiently at the same wavelength.
Therefore assertion is true.
The reason provided references Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which states that for a body in thermal equilibrium, the absorptivity (the ability to absorb radiation) is equal to its emissivity (the ability to emit radiation) at a specific wavelength. This law applies to all materials and is fundamental in thermodynamics and radiative transfer.
Reason is the correct explanation of assertion

questions.q:
Heat energy of 184 kJ is given to ice of mass 600 g at -12 °C, Specific heat of ice is 2222.3 J kg–1 °C–1 and latent heat of ice is 336 kJ kg–1.

(A) Final temperature of system will be 0 °C

(B) Final temperature of the system will be greater than 0 °C

(C) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of 5 : 1

(D) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of  1 : 5

(E) The final system will have water only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Given:

∆Q=184×103 J,

m=0.600 kg at -12 °C,

S=2222.3 J kg–1 °C–1 and

L=336×103J kg-1

Heat required to convert ice from –12 °C to ice at 0 °C will be, 

Q1=0.600×2222.3×12=16000.56 J

Remaining heat Q=184000-16000.56

= 167999.44 J

Heat required to melt ice completely at 0 °C,

Q2 = 0.600 × 336000 = 201600 J needed which is more than Q, so 100% ice is not melted.

For amount of melted ice, we can write

167999.44=m×336000⇒m= 0.4999 kg

∴ mass of water =0.4999 kg

Mass of ice remaining = 0.1001

∴ Ratio =0.10010.4999≈1:5

questions.solution:
Methods of Heat Transfer:
Conduction:
- The heat transfer through direct physical contact is known as conduction.
- Heat transferred from the electric burner of a stove to the bottom of a pan is transferred by conduction.
Radiation:
- When electromagnetic radiation is emitted or absorbed to transfer the heat or When heat is transferred in the form of electromagnetic waves is known as radiation.
- Electromagnetic radiation includes microwaves, radio waves, infrared radiation, visible light, ultraviolet radiation, gamma rays, and X-rays.
- The method does not require any medium so heat from the sun reaches us by this method.
Convection
- It is heat transfer by the movement of its molecules.
- It occurs only in fluids (liquid and gas) not in solids because solid particles can not move from one place to another.
- For example, in a pot boiling water on the stove, or in thunderstorms, where hot air rises up to the base of the clouds.
- Sea breeze and land breeze occurs due to convection.

- d. Evaporation \(\rightarrow\) r. Slow
